content: Pneumococcal disease encompasses various types, each with distinct symptoms, risk factors, and methods of prevention. The symptoms of pneumococcal disease vary depending on the specific part of the body that is affected. Vaccination is essential for young children, older adults, and individuals with certain underlying health conditions to prevent pneumococcal disease. For healthcare providers, a clinical overview includes understanding the causative agent, identifying risk factors, and recognizing the modes of transmission of pneumococcal disease. Clinical guidance is available to assist in the testing, prevention, and management of this condition. The clinical features of pneumococcal disease include its presentation and potential complications. Public health professionals monitor invasive pneumococcal disease trends using two surveillance systems. Additionally, pneumococcal bacteria have demonstrated resistance to one or more antibiotics in numerous cases, posing challenges to treatment. Further resources are available through the CDC's Streptococcus Laboratory.
